---
title: "Start with what a number counts"
description: "Why a workforce measure needs a population and a time boundary before it needs a chart."
content-type: essay
author: OWAS

A headcount can refer to people, contracts, or assignments. Each can be useful, but they answer different questions. A chart label alone rarely tells readers which object was counted.

The first task is to state the population and unit. The next is to explain time: a snapshot at one instant behaves differently from a count of everyone present during a month.

Only then can a reader interpret change. A rising series may reflect more people, a broader reporting boundary, or corrected source records. Good documentation gives readers a way to distinguish those explanations.

The [illustrative headcount definition](../../standards/headcount/point-in-time-headcount/index.qmd) makes these choices explicit. This essay explains the motivation; the reference page records the calculation contract.
